description:
FILED s459an (agent AN, round 16), the measured residue of #861.

`\` DISTRIBUTES OVER A SLICE in perl: a slice is a LIST, so `\@A[0,1]` is a
two-element list of SCALAR refs, one per element -- not one ref to anything.
PCL answers a ONE-element list in every spelling.

PROBED (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, one file):

    my %H=(a=>1,b=>2); my @A=(10,20,30); my $h=\%H; my $a=\@A;
    my @s = \@A[0,1];        # perl 2 SCALAR 10 20   PCL 1 SCALAR 20
    my @s = \@H{qw(a b)};    # perl 2 SCALAR 1 2     PCL 1 SCALAR 2
    my @s = \@$a[0,1];       # perl 2 SCALAR 10 20   PCL 1 SCALAR 20
    my @s = \@$h{qw(a b)};   # perl 2 SCALAR 1 2     PCL 1 SCALAR 2
    my @s = \@{$a}[0,1];     # perl 2 SCALAR         PCL 1 SCALAR
    my @s = \@{$h}{qw(a b)}; # perl 2 SCALAR         PCL 1 SCALAR

SILENT WRONG: the count is wrong AND the surviving ref is the LAST element,
so `my ($p,$q) = \@A[0,1]` leaves $q undef and $p pointing at $A[1].

WHERE IT IS NOT.  This is NOT the #861 cast-run bug: the NAMED spellings
`\@A[0,1]` / `\@H{...}` carry no deref cast at all and are wrong identically,
and #861's fix leaves them byte-identical.  The distribute machinery lives in
`Pl::ExprToCL::gen_prefix_op_form`, gated on the `backslash_paren_list`
metadata -- i.e. PCL distributes `\` only over an explicit `\( LIST )`, and a
bare slice operand never sets that flag.  perl's rule is about the operand
being a LIST, and a slice is one.

ONE SIDE EFFECT OF #861 TO KNOW ABOUT: the `@$ref[...]` / `@$ref{...}`
spellings used to answer one ARRAY ref (the `\` was swallowed into the cast
run and the node came out a plain element access); they now answer one SCALAR
ref, i.e. they JOINED this family instead of being wrong in their own way.
Neither is perl; the new answer has the right ref KIND and the same wrong
count as its five siblings, which is why it is one task and not two.

FIX SHAPE (unmeasured): the `\`-operand test in gen_prefix_op_form should ask
"does this operand produce a LIST" rather than "was it written with parens" --
the slice node types (slice_a_acc / slice_h_acc / kv_slice_*) are exactly the
extra answers, and `_gen_backslash_multi_term_form` is the emitter already in
place for the distributed result.  Probe the NEGATIVES: `\@A` and `\%H` and
`\@$a` must stay ONE ARRAY/HASH ref (they are not slices), and `\@A[0]` --
a one-element slice -- is a one-element LIST in perl, not a bare scalar ref.

BAR: the six spellings above plus those four negatives, all vs perl; the
shape occurs in no census population (measured s459an: every `\@...[` hit in
perl-tests, perl's own t/ and the cpan board is an escaped `\$` inside a
string), so probes and guard rows are the bar under the s371 rule.


=== SHIPPED s460ap (agent AP, round 17).  #892 CLOSED.

THE FIX IS ONE PREDICATE AND THREE CALLERS, in Pl/ExprToCL.pm.
`_is_refgen_spread_node` answers "does applying `\` to this TERM yield one ref
per element", and exactly two shapes say yes: the range operator (already
handled, moved in here) and the four SLICE node types (slice_a_acc /
slice_h_acc / kv_slice_h_acc / kv_slice_a_acc).  Its three callers:
  1. gen_prefix_op_form's `\` gate -- was `does this operand carry the
     backslash_paren_list metadata`, i.e. "was it written with parens"; it now
     ALSO fires for a bare slice, which is the question perl asks;
  2. _is_list_node_for_refgen (the single-child \( ) test), so `\(@A[0,1])`
     stops collapsing to \$A[1];
  3. _gen_backslash_multi_term_form's per-term test, which was keyed on `..`
     alone -- 'range' is renamed 'spread' there because it is no longer only a
     range.

THE TASK'S SHAPE WAS RIGHT AND ITS SCOPE WAS TWO SPELLINGS SHORT.  Beyond the
six the task lists, the PARENTHESIZED spellings were wrong too, and no one had
looked: `\(@A[0,1])` answered ONE ref (the single-child arm collapsed it to
`\$A[1]`) and `\($A[0], @A[1,2])` answered TWO where perl gives THREE (the
multi-term walk took the slice on its 'single' arm).  Also measured: the
distributed refs must ALIAS the container (`${$s[0]} = 99` writes $A[0]) --
PCL's answer wrote nothing, since the one ref pointed at a scalar-context
reduction.  All fixed by the same predicate.

WHAT MUST NOT SPREAD, and this is the half that constrains the fix (probed
perl 5.40.3): an array or hash VARIABLE.  perlref's spread is the SPECIAL case
for a parenthesized list that is exactly one aggregate, so `\(@A)` is three
scalar refs but `\(@A, $x)` is (ARRAY, SCALAR), `\(@A, @B)` is (ARRAY, ARRAY)
and `\(%H, $x)` is (HASH, SCALAR).  That is why the new predicate is NOT
"_is_list_node_for_refgen" -- replacing the multi-term walk's test with the
wider one would have broken all three.

BAR MET.  42 probe rows over three files, all BYTE-IDENTICAL to perl: the six
task spellings + postfix-deref `\$a->@[0,1]` + `\@A[0..2]` + the one-element
slice `\@A[0]` + both kv spellings + the two paren spellings + write-through +
scalar context + ten negatives.  Emission A/B over FOUR populations: 111
perl-tests (1 diff), perl's own t/ 605 (3 diffs), lib 22 (0), cpan board 383
(0), RCDIFF 0 everywhere.  Every diff explained AND its verdict measured:
  - perl-tests/kvaslice.t:86 + t/op/kvaslice.t + t/op/kvhslice.t -- literally
    the "# ref of a slice produces list" test.  Verdicts UNCHANGED (17/0,
    24/14, 20/18) because the rows had been passing BY ACCIDENT: PCL's `$$_`
    on the one wrong ref flattened the whole kv-slice, so `join(':', map {$$_}
    @tmp)` produced the right string from the wrong structure.
  - t/op/for-many.t -- COMPILER-GENERATED perl: the n-at-a-time foreach
    lowering writes `push @__PCL_FL0, \@__PCL_PD0[scalar @__PCL_PD0] while ...`,
    a ONE-element slice.  Old `(p-backslash (p-list-scalar (p-aslice ...)))`,
    new `(p-refgen-list (p-aslice ...))`; push flattens the one-element vector,
    so behaviour is identical and the verdict is (measured) 63/8 both ways.
Gate green; full sweep GATE clean.

GUARD: Pl/t/list-slice-01.t rows 11-13 (10 -> 13).  11 = the eleven positive
spellings, 12 = the write-through alias, 13 = the INVERSE, which PASSES ON THE
BASE COMPILER TOO (that is what proves the widened predicate did not swallow
the aggregate spellings).  Inverse-verified: 11-12 fail on base, 13 passes.
subject: `\` does not DISTRIBUTE over a slice: `\@A[0,1]` is one ref, perl gives a list of one ref per element (#861 residue)
